author: Taylor Daugherty
title: Connecticut man sentenced to 30 years for attempting to entice child for sexual exploitation - NewsBreak
text: JACKSONVILLE, Florida — Andrew Thomas Bull, a 37-year-old from Tolland, Connecticut, has been sentenced to 30 years in federal prison for attempting to entice an 11-year-old child to engage in sexually explicit conduct. The sentence was handed down by Chief United States District Judge Marcia Morales Howard. Bull, also known as Andrew Thomas Picard, was ordered to serve a 10-year term of supervised release and forfeit the electronic device used in the offense. Previously convicted of importation and possession of child pornography in Connecticut in 2013, Bull was on court-ordered probation when arrested on May 25, 2023, according to court documents. The investigation began on November 15, 2022, when an FBI agent in Jacksonville conducted an online undercover operation to identify adults seeking sexual activity with children. Bull, using the alias "brdr1066," contacted the agent and confirmed his desire to engage with the child, sending explicit photos and soliciting pornographic images, according to the FBI. Upon his arrest, a search of Bull's cellphone revealed at least 15 videos and 40 photos depicting child sexual abuse, including an infant. "Protecting kids from predators is among the most important work that we do at the FBI," said Jason Carley, Special Agent in Charge of the FBI Jacksonville Division. "Let this case be a warning - the FBI is relentless in our efforts to identify and stop child predators from abusing our kids." The case was investigated by the FBI in Jacksonville and New Haven, Connecticut, and prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorneys D. Rodney Brown and Kelly S. Milliron. It was part of Project Safe Childhood, a Department of Justice initiative to combat child sexual exploitation and abuse.
